title: Catalpa: Ancient Catalpa Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: A tree of heart-shaped leaves, white flowers and long bean pods. Leiden's leaning catalpa is held up by cables, and Staten Island's has a 3.75 metre trunk.
intro: Catalpa is an American tree that Europe and the American cities took up for its heart-shaped leaves, its June flowers and the long pods that hang on through winter. In Leiden, the catalpa at the Hortus Botanicus leans over the canal behind the glasshouse and is held up by cables run across to a zelkova in the Japanese garden; the register dates it to 1820, inside a band of 1820 to 1830. On Staten Island, a catalpa behind the tin shop at Historic Richmond Town has a trunk about 3.75 metres round, and NYC Parks named it to its Great Trees list in 2024. In Washington, two catalpas flank the Survey Lodge on the Mall, planted around 1902 along an oval carriage road beside a building made from the Washington Monument's leftover stone.
